title: FESEN/CSTB sit-in at the education ministry over teachers’ and education workers’ demands
location: Cotonou, at the Ministry of Secondary Education in the administrative tower; exact area within the building unknown
scope: reported single union sit-in; relationship to a separately announced AME meeting at the ministry on the same date is unresolved
organizer: Fédération des syndicats de l’éducation nationale (FESEN), affiliated with the Confédération des syndicats des travailleurs du Bénin (CSTB)
participants_original: Not stated in the opened report; teachers and administrative staff are described as participants.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened report confirms an actual sit-in by teachers and refers to participants/manifestants, but gives no numerical attendance or estimate. At least 50 is not established; eligibility remains pending_threshold.

occurrence_and_date.summary: Le Matinal states that FESEN/CSTB teachers held a sit-in in Cotonou on Wednesday 20 March 2024.

location.summary: The article identifies Cotonou and says the sit-in was held at the administrative tower/ministry of education; exact gathering area is not stated.

organizer_and_scope.summary: The report identifies FESEN, affiliated with CSTB, and describes one sit-in; relation to the concurrent AME meeting remains unresolved.

demands.summary: The reproduced declaration lists unpaid school-entry bonuses, teacher advancement/training claims, CNSS deductions, cancellation of disciplinary explanations for strikers, and postponement of professional elections. Code labor pay/work conditions and political process.

participants_original.summary: The article says teachers gathered and calls them participants/manifestants but provides no count or crowd estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance number or qualifying estimate appears in the opened report, so the 50-person requirement is unknown.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not describe violence by participants in this sit-in.

state_response.summary: No event-specific state response to the sit-in is reported. The article recounts silence and disciplinary explanations after the earlier 7 March strike; those are not attributed to the 20 March sit-in.

notes: Search lead was verified by one opened Le Matinal report. Its body includes a reproduced FESEN/CSTB declaration, so the account and declaration are not independent corroboration. The source reports a prior 24-hour strike on 7 March and a distinct sit-in on 20 March; do not merge them. Official baseline remains pending.
open_questions: Can an independent contemporary source establish attendance of at least 50 at the 20 March sit-in?
Was the sit-in one gathering with the separately announced AME meeting, or a distinct action?
What was the sit-in’s physical end time/date, and was there an event-specific state response?
